20.e: And it should be done like this. One is either appointed through oneself or through another. And how is one appointed through oneself? A competent and capable nun should inform the Sangha:

20.s: ‘suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, ahaṁ itthannāmā itthannāmaṁ anusāseyyan’ti.
20.e: ‘Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with venerable so-and-so. If the Sangha is ready, I so-and-so will instruct so-and-so.’

20.s: Evaṁ attanāva attānaṁ sammannitabbaṁ.
Kathañca parāya parā sammannitabbā? Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo—
20.e: And how is one appointed through another? A competent and capable nun should inform the Sangha:

20.s: ‘suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, itthannāmā itthannāmaṁ anusāseyyā’ti.
20.e: ‘Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with venerable so-and-so. If the Sangha is ready, so-and-so will instruct so-and-so.’

20.s: Evaṁ parāya parā sammannitabbā.

Tāya sammatāya bhikkhuniyā upasampadāpekkhaṁ upasaṅkamitvā evamassa vacanīyā— ‘suṇasi itthannāme. Ayaṁ te saccakālo, bhūtakālo. Yaṁ jātaṁ taṁ saṅghamajjhe pucchante santaṁ atthīti vattabbaṁ, asantaṁ natthīti vattabbaṁ. Mā kho vitthāyi, mā kho maṅku ahosi. Evaṁ taṁ pucchissanti— nasi animittā, nasi nimittamattā, nasi alohitā, nasi dhuvalohitā, nasi dhuvacoḷā, nasi paggharantī, nasi sikharaṇī, nasi itthipaṇḍakā, nasi vepurisikā, nasi sambhinnā, nasi ubhatobyañjanā? Santi te evarūpā ābādhā— kuṭṭhaṁ, gaṇḍo, kilāso, soso, apamāro? Manussāsi, itthīsi, bhujissāsi, aṇaṇāsi, nasi rājabhaṭī? Anuññātāsi mātāpitūhi, sāmikena? Paripuṇṇavīsativassāsi, paripuṇṇaṁ te pattacīvaraṁ, kiṁnāmāsi, kānāmā te pavattinī’ti?
20.e: The appointed nun should go to the one seeking the full ordination and say this: ‘Listen, so-and-so. Now is the time for you to tell the truth. You will be asked in the midst of the Sangha about various matters. If something is true, you should say, “Yes,” and if it’s not, you should say, “No.” Don’t be embarrassed or humiliated. This is what they’ll ask you: “Do you lack genitals? Are your genitals incomplete? Do you not menstruate? Do you menstruate continuously? Do you always wear a menstruation pad? Are you incontinent? Do you have genital prolapse? Do you lack sexual organs? Are you manlike? Do you have fistula? Are you a gynandromorph? Do you have any of these diseases: leprosy, abscesses, mild leprosy, tuberculosis, or epilepsy? Are you human? Are you a woman? Are you free from slavery? Are you free from debt? Are you employed by the king? Do you have permission from your parents and husband? Are you twenty years old? Do you have a full set of bowl and robes? What’s your name? What’s the name of your mentor?”’”

20.s: Ekato āgacchanti.
20.e: They then returned to the Sangha together.

20.s: Na ekato āgantabbaṁ.
20.e: “They shouldn’t return together.

20.s: Anusāsikāya paṭhamataraṁ āgantvā saṅgho ñāpetabbo—
20.e: The instructor should return first and inform the Sangha:

20.s: ‘suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Anusiṭṭhā sā mayā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, itthannāmā āgaccheyyā’ti.
20.e: ‘Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with venerable so-and-so. She has been instructed by me. If the Sangha is ready, so-and-so should come.’

20.s: ‘Āgacchāhī’ti vattabbā. Ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ kārāpetvā bhikkhunīnaṁ pāde vandāpetvā ukkuṭikaṁ nisīdāpetvā añjaliṁ paggaṇhāpetvā upasampadaṁ yācāpetabbā—
20.e: And she should be told to come. She should then arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, pay respect at the feet of the nuns, squat on her heels, and raise her joined palms. She should then ask for the full ordination:

20.s: ‘saṅghaṁ, ayye, upasampadaṁ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṁ, ayye, saṅgho anukampaṁ upādāya. Dutiyampi, ayye, saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṁ, ayye, saṅgho anukampaṁ upādāya. Tatiyampi, ayye, saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṁ, ayye, saṅgho anukampaṁ upādāyā’ti.
20.e: ‘Venerables, I ask the Sangha for the full ordination. Please lift me up out of compassion. For the second time, venerables, I ask the Sangha for the full ordination. Please lift me up out of compassion. For the third time, venerables, I ask the Sangha for the full ordination. Please lift me up out of compassion.’

20.s: Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo—
20.e: A competent and capable nun should then inform the Sangha:

20.s: ‘Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṁ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, ahaṁ itthannāmaṁ antarāyike dhamme puccheyyanti.
20.e: ‘Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with venerable so-and-so. If the Sangha is ready, I so-and-so will ask so-and-so about the obstacles.

20.s: Suṇasi itthannāme. Ayaṁ te saccakālo, bhūtakālo. Yaṁ jātaṁ taṁ pucchāmi santaṁ atthīti vattabbaṁ, asantaṁ natthīti vattabbaṁ. Nasi animittā …pe… kiṁnāmāsi, kānāmā te pavattinī’ti.
20.e: Listen, so-and-so. Now is the time for you to tell the truth. I will ask you about various matters. If something is true, you should say, “Yes,” and if it’s not, you should say, “No.” So: Do you lack genitals? Are your genitals incomplete? Do you not menstruate? Do you menstruate continuously? Do you always wear a menstruation pad? Are you incontinent? Do you have genital prolapse? Do you lack sexual organs? Are you manlike? Do you have fistula? Are you a gynandromorph? Do you have any of these diseases: leprosy, abscesses, mild leprosy, tuberculosis, or epilepsy? Are you human? Are you a woman? Are you free from slavery? Are you free from debt? Are you employed by the king? Do you have permission from your parents and husband? Are you twenty years old? Do you have a full set of bowl and robes? What’s your name? What’s the name of your mentor?’

20.s: Byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo—
20.e: A competent and capable nun should inform the Sangha:

20.s: ‘Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṁ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Parisuddhā antarāyikehi dhammehi, paripuṇṇassā pattacīvaraṁ. Itthannāmā saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācati itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, saṅgho itthannāmaṁ upasampādeyya itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā. Esā ñatti.
20.e: ‘Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with venerable so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and her bowl and robes are complete. So-and-so is asking the Sangha for the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. If the Sangha is ready, it should give so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. This is the motion.

20.s: Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṁ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Parisuddhā antarāyikehi dhammehi, paripuṇṇassā pattacīvaraṁ. Itthannāmā saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācati itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā. Saṅgho itthannāmaṁ upasampādeti itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya upasampadā itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.
20.e: Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with venerable so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and her bowl and robes are complete. So-and-so is asking the Sangha for the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. The Sangha gives so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. Any nun who approves of giving so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor should remain silent. Any nun who doesn’t approve should speak up.

20.s: Dutiyampi etamatthaṁ vadāmi …pe…
20.e: For the second time, I speak on this matter. Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with venerable so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and her bowl and robes are complete. So-and-so is asking the Sangha for the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. The Sangha gives so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. Any nun who approves of giving so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor should remain silent. Any nun who doesn’t approve should speak up.

20.s: tatiyampi etamatthaṁ vadāmi— suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Ayaṁ itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Parisuddhā antarāyikehi dhammehi, paripuṇṇassā pattacīvaraṁ. Itthannāmā saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācati itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā. Saṅgho itthannāmaṁ upasampādeti itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya upasampadā itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.
20.e: For the third time, I speak on this matter. Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with venerable so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and her bowl and robes are complete. So-and-so is asking the Sangha for the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. The Sangha gives so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. Any nun who approves of giving so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor should remain silent. Any nun who doesn’t approve should speak up.

20.s: Upasampannā saṅghena itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya pavattiniyā. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmī’ti.
20.e: The Sangha has given so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. The Sangha approves and is therefore silent. I will remember it thus.’

20.s: Tāvadeva taṁ ādāya bhikkhusaṅghaṁ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ kārāpetvā bhikkhūnaṁ pāde vandāpetvā ukkuṭikaṁ nisīdāpetvā añjaliṁ paggaṇhāpetvā upasampadaṁ yācāpetabbā—
20.e: Straightaway she should be taken to the Sangha of monks. She should arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, pay respect at the feet of the monks, squat on her heels, and raise her joined palms. She should then ask for the full ordination:

20.s: ‘ahaṁ, ayyā, itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā; saṅghaṁ, ayyā, upasampadaṁ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṁ, ayyā, saṅgho anukampaṁ upādāya.
20.e: ‘Venerables, I’m seeking the full ordination with venerable so-and-so. I’m free from obstacles and have been fully ordained on one side in the Sangha of nuns. I ask the Sangha for the full ordination. Please lift me up out of compassion.

20.s: Ahaṁ, ayyā, itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Dutiyampi, ayyā, saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṁ, ayyā, saṅgho anukampaṁ upādāya.
20.e: Venerables, I’m seeking the full ordination with venerable so-and-so. I’m free from obstacles and have been fully ordained on one side in the Sangha of nuns. For the second time, I ask the Sangha for the full ordination. Please lift me up out of compassion.

20.s: Ahaṁ, ayyā, itthannāmā itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Tatiyampi, ayyā, saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācāmi. Ullumpatu maṁ, ayyā, saṅgho anukampaṁ upādāyā’ti.
20.e: Venerables, I’m seeking the full ordination with venerable so-and-so. I’m free from obstacles and have been fully ordained on one side in the Sangha of nuns. For the third time, I ask the Sangha for the full ordination. Please lift me up out of compassion.’

20.s: Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo—
20.e: A competent and capable monk should inform the Sangha:

20.s: ‘Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṁ itthannāmā itthannāmāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Itthannāmā saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācati itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, saṅgho itthannāmaṁ upasampādeyya, itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Esā ñatti.
20.e: ‘Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and has been fully ordained on one side in the Sangha of nuns. So-and-so is asking the Sangha for the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. If the Sangha is ready, it should give so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. This is the motion.

20.s: Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṁ itthannāmā itthannāmāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Itthannāmā saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācati itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Saṅgho itthannāmaṁ upasampādeti itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmāya upasampadā itthannāmāya pavattiniyā, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.
20.e: Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and has been fully ordained on one side in the Sangha of nuns. So-and-so is asking the Sangha for the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. The Sangha gives so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. Any monk who approves of giving so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor should remain silent. Any monk who doesn’t approve should speak up.

20.s: Dutiyampi etamatthaṁ vadāmi …pe…
20.e: For the second time, I speak on this matter. Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and has been fully ordained on one side in the Sangha of nuns. So-and-so is asking the Sangha for the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. The Sangha gives so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. Any monk who approves of giving so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor should remain silent. Any monk who doesn’t approve should speak up.

20.s: tatiyampi etamatthaṁ vadāmi— suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Ayaṁ itthannāmā itthannāmāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Itthannāmā saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācati itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Saṅgho itthannāmaṁ upasampādeti itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmāya upasampadā itthannāmāya pavattiniyā, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.
20.e: For the third time, I speak on this matter. Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and has been fully ordained on one side in the Sangha of nuns. So-and-so is asking the Sangha for the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. The Sangha gives so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. Any monk who approves of giving so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor should remain silent. Any monk who doesn’t approve should speak up.

20.s: Upasampannā saṅghena itthannāmā itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmī’ti.
20.e: The Sangha has given so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. The Sangha approves and is therefore silent. I will remember it thus.’

20.s: Tāvadeva chāyā metabbā, utuppamāṇaṁ ācikkhitabbaṁ, divasabhāgo ācikkhitabbo, saṅgīti ācikkhitabbā, bhikkhuniyo vattabbā— imissā tayo ca nissaye, aṭṭha ca akaraṇīyāni ācikkheyyāthā”ti.
20.e: Straightaway the time should be noted and the date should be pointed out. These should be declared jointly to everyone. The nuns should be told to point out the three supports and the eight things not to be done.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo bhattagge āsanaṁ saṅkasāyantiyo kālaṁ vītināmesuṁ. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: On one occasion the right time for eating passed while the nuns were trying to find the right seats in the dining hall. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, aṭṭhannaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ yathāvuḍḍhaṁ, avasesānaṁ yathāgatikan”ti.
20.e: “I allow eight nuns to be seated according to seniority, but the rest according to their time of arrival.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo— “bhagavatā anuññātaṁ aṭṭhannaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ yathāvuḍḍhaṁ, avasesānaṁ yathāgatikan”ti— sabbattha aṭṭheva bhikkhuniyo yathāvuḍḍhaṁ paṭibāhanti, avasesāyo yathāgatikaṁ. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: When they heard about the Buddha’s allowance, eight nuns reserved places everywhere according to seniority, the rest getting places according to their time of arrival. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhattagge aṭṭhannaṁ bhikkhunīnaṁ yathāvuḍḍhaṁ, avasesānaṁ yathāgatikaṁ; aññattha sabbattha yathāvuḍḍhaṁ na paṭibāhitabbaṁ. Yā paṭibāheyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
20.e: “I allow eight nuns to be seated in the dining hall according to seniority and the rest according to their time of arrival, but not anywhere else. If a nun makes a reservation anywhere apart from the dining hall, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo na pavārenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: At that time the nuns did not do the invitation ceremony. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā na pavāretabbaṁ. Yā na pavāreyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.
20.e: “A nun should do the invitation ceremony. If she doesn’t, she should be dealt with according to the rule.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo attanā pavāretvā bhikkhusaṅghaṁ na pavārenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: At that time the nuns did the invitation ceremony among themselves, but not with the Sangha of monks. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā attanā pavāretvā bhikkhusaṅgho na pavāretabbo. Yā na pavāreyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.
20.e: “After doing the invitation ceremony with the nuns, a nun should do the invitation ceremony with the monks. If she doesn’t, she should be dealt with according to the rule.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ ekato pavārentiyo kolāhalaṁ akaṁsu. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: The nuns did their invitation ceremony together with the monks. They made a racket. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā bhikkhūhi saddhiṁ ekato pavāretabbaṁ. Yā pavāreyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
20.e: “The nuns shouldn’t do their invitation ceremony together with the monks. Any nun who does commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo purebhattaṁ pavārentiyo kālaṁ vītināmesuṁ. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: On one occasion when the nuns did the invitation ceremony before the meal, they did not finish until after the time for eating. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pacchābhattaṁ pavāretun”ti.
20.e: “I allow the nuns to do the invitation ceremony after the meal.”

20.s: Pacchābhattaṁ pavārentiyo vikāle ahesuṁ. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: Doing the invitation ceremony after the meal, they did not finish until it was too late in the evening. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ajjatanā bhikkhunisaṅghaṁ pavāretvā aparajju bhikkhusaṅghaṁ pavāretun”ti.
20.e: “I allow the nuns to do the invitation ceremony among themselves on one day and with the monks on the following day.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena sabbo bhikkhunisaṅgho pavārento kolāhalaṁ akāsi. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: At that time the whole Sangha of nuns did the invitation ceremony. They made a racket. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekaṁ bhikkhuniṁ byattaṁ paṭibalaṁ sammannituṁ— bhikkhunisaṅghassa atthāya bhikkhusaṅghaṁ pavāretuṁ. Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbā. Paṭhamaṁ bhikkhunī yācitabbā, yācitvā byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo—
20.e: “I allow the nuns to appoint one capable and competent nun to do the invitation ceremony with the Sangha of monks on behalf of the Sangha of nuns. She should be appointed like this. First a nun should be asked, and then a competent and capable nun should inform the Sangha:

20.s: ‘Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, saṅgho itthannāmaṁ bhikkhuniṁ sammanneyya bhikkhunisaṅghassa atthāya bhikkhusaṅghaṁ pavāretuṁ. Esā ñatti.
20.e: ‘Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. If the Sangha is ready, it should appoint nun so-and-so to do the invitation ceremony with the Sangha of monks on behalf of the Sangha of nuns. This is the motion.

20.s: Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṁ bhikkhuniṁ sammannati bhikkhunisaṅghassa atthāya bhikkhusaṅghaṁ pavāretuṁ. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā sammuti bhikkhunisaṅghassa atthāya bhikkhusaṅghaṁ pavāretuṁ, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.
20.e: Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. The Sangha appoints nun so-and-so to do the invitation ceremony with the Sangha of monks on behalf of the Sangha of nuns. Any nun who approves of appointing nun so-and-so to do the invitation ceremony with the Sangha of monks on behalf of the Sangha of nuns should remain silent. Any nun who doesn’t approve should speak up.

20.s: Sammatā saṅghena itthannāmā bhikkhunī bhikkhunisaṅghassa atthāya bhikkhusaṅghaṁ pavāretuṁ. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmī’ti.
20.e: The Sangha has appointed nun so-and-so to do the invitation ceremony with the Sangha of monks on behalf of the Sangha of nuns. The Sangha approves and is therefore silent. I will remember it thus.’

20.s: Tāya sammatāya bhikkhuniyā bhikkhunisaṅghaṁ ādāya bhikkhusaṅghaṁ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ karitvā bhikkhūnaṁ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṁ nisīditvā añjaliṁ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo— ‘bhikkhunisaṅgho, ayyā, bhikkhusaṅghaṁ pavāreti— diṭṭhena vā, sutena vā parisaṅkāya vā. Vadatu, ayyā, bhikkhusaṅgho bhikkhunisaṅghaṁ anukampaṁ upādāya, passanto paṭikarissati. Dutiyampi, ayyā …pe… tatiyampi, ayyā, bhikkhunisaṅgho bhikkhusaṅghaṁ pavāreti— diṭṭhena vā, sutena vā, parisaṅkāya vā. Vadatu, ayyā, bhikkhusaṅgho bhikkhunisaṅghaṁ anukampaṁ upādāya, passanto paṭikarissatī’”ti.
20.e: The appointed nun should take the Sangha of nuns to the Sangha of monks. She should then arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, squat on her heels, raise her joined palms, and say: ‘Venerables, the Sangha of nuns invites the Sangha of monks to correct it concerning what you’ve seen, heard, or suspect. Please correct the Sangha of nuns, venerables, out of compassion. If the Sangha of nuns sees a fault, it will make amends. For the second time, the Sangha of nuns invites the Sangha of monks to correct it concerning what you’ve seen, heard, or suspect. Please correct the Sangha of nuns, venerables, out of compassion. If the Sangha of nuns sees a fault, it will make amends. For the third time, the Sangha of nuns invites the Sangha of monks to correct it concerning what you’ve seen, heard, or suspect. Please correct the Sangha of nuns, venerables, out of compassion. If the Sangha of nuns sees a fault, it will make amends.’”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo bhikkhūnaṁ uposathaṁ ṭhapenti, pavāraṇaṁ ṭhapenti, savacanīyaṁ karonti, anuvādaṁ paṭṭhapenti, okāsaṁ kārenti, codenti, sārenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: At that time the nuns canceled the monks’ observance-day ceremony and their invitation ceremony; they directed them, gave them instructions, got permission from them to correct them, accused them of offenses, and reminded them of offenses. They told the Buddha.
20.t: Mutual authority between monks and nuns

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā bhikkhussa uposatho ṭhapetabbo; ṭhapitopi aṭṭhapito; ṭhapentiyā āpatti dukkaṭassa.
20.e: “A nun shouldn’t cancel the observance-day ceremony of a monk. If she does, it’s not valid, and she commits an offense of wrong conduct.

20.s: Na pavāraṇā ṭhapetabbā; ṭhapitāpi aṭṭhapitā; ṭhapentiyā āpatti dukkaṭassa.
20.e: A nun shouldn’t cancel the invitation ceremony of a monk. If she does, it’s not valid, and she commits an offense of wrong conduct.

20.s: Na savacanīyaṁ kātabbaṁ; katampi akataṁ; karontiyā āpatti dukkaṭassa.
20.e: A nun shouldn’t direct a monk. If she does, it’s not valid, and she commits an offense of wrong conduct.

20.s: Na anuvādo paṭṭhapetabbo; paṭṭhapitopi appaṭṭhapito; paṭṭhapentiyā āpatti dukkaṭassa.
20.e: A nun shouldn’t give instructions to a monk. If she does, it’s not valid, and she commits an offense of wrong conduct.

20.s: Na okāso kāretabbo; kāritopi akārito; kārentiyā āpatti dukkaṭassa.
20.e: A nun shouldn’t ask permission from a monk to correct him. If she does, it’s not valid, and she commits an offense of wrong conduct.

20.s: Na codetabbo; coditopi acodito; codentiyā āpatti dukkaṭassa.
20.e: A nun shouldn’t accuse a monk of an offense. If she does, it’s not valid, and she commits an offense of wrong conduct.

20.s: Na sāretabbo; sāritopi asārito; sārentiyā āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
20.e: A nun shouldn’t remind a monk of an offense. If she does, it’s not valid, and she commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhū bhikkhunīnaṁ uposathaṁ ṭhapenti, pavāraṇaṁ ṭhapenti, savacanīyaṁ karonti, anuvādaṁ paṭṭhapenti, okāsaṁ kārenti, codenti, sārenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: At that time the monks canceled the nuns’ observance-day ceremony and their invitation ceremony; they directed them, gave them instructions, got permission from them to correct them, accused them of offenses, and reminded them of offenses. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā bhikkhuniyā uposathaṁ ṭhapetuṁ; ṭhapitopi suṭṭhapito; ṭhapentassa anāpatti.
20.e: “A monk may cancel the observance-day ceremony of a nun. If he does, it’s valid, and there’s no offense for him.

20.s: Pavāraṇaṁ ṭhapetuṁ; ṭhapitāpi suṭṭhapitā; ṭhapentassa anāpatti.
20.e: A monk may cancel the invitation ceremony of a nun. If he does, it’s valid, and there’s no offense for him.

20.s: Savacanīyaṁ kātuṁ; katampi sukataṁ; karontassa anāpatti.
20.e: A monk may direct a nun. If he does, it’s valid, and there’s no offense for him.

20.s: Anuvādaṁ paṭṭhapetuṁ; paṭṭhapitopi suppaṭṭhapito; paṭṭhapentassa anāpatti.
20.e: A monk may give instructions to a nun. If he does, it’s valid, and there’s no offense for him.

20.s: Okāsaṁ kāretuṁ; kāritopi sukārito; kārentassa anāpatti.
20.e: A monk may ask permission from a nun to correct her. If he does, it’s valid, and there’s no offense for him.

20.s: Codetuṁ; coditāpi sucoditā; codentassa anāpatti.
20.e: A monk may accuse a nun of an offense. If he does, it’s valid, and there’s no offense for him.

20.s: Sāretuṁ; sāritāpi susāritā; sārentassa anāpattī”ti.
20.e: A monk may remind a nun of an offense. If he does, it’s valid, and there’s no offense for him.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo yānena yāyanti— itthiyuttenapi purisantarena, purisayuttenapi itthantarena. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti …pe… seyyathāpi gaṅgāmahiyāyā”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: At that time the nuns from the group of six traveled in vehicles, sometimes pulled by women with men inside, at other times pulled by men with women inside. People complained and criticized them, “You’d think they were at the Ganges festival!” They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā yānena yāyitabbaṁ. Yā yāyeyya, yathādhammo kāretabbo”ti.
20.e: “A nun shouldn’t travel in a vehicle. If she does, she should be dealt with according to the rule.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī gilānā hoti, na sakkoti padasā gantuṁ. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: Soon afterwards there was a sick nun who was unable to go on foot. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, gilānāya yānan”ti.
20.e: “I allow a vehicle for one who is sick.”

20.s: Atha kho bhikkhunīnaṁ etadahosi— “itthiyuttaṁ nu kho, purisayuttaṁ nu kho”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: The nuns thought, “A vehicle pulled by women or by men?” They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, itthiyuttaṁ purisayuttaṁ hatthavaṭṭakan”ti.
20.e: “I allow a rickshaw pulled either by men or by women.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarissā bhikkhuniyā yānugghātena bāḷhataraṁ aphāsu ahosi. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: Soon afterwards a certain nun was even more uncomfortable when jolted around in a vehicle. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sivikaṁ pāṭaṅkin”ti.
20.e: “I allow a palanquin and a litter.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena aḍḍhakāsī gaṇikā bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā hoti. Sā ca sāvatthiṁ gantukāmā hoti— “bhagavato santike upasampajjissāmī”ti. Assosuṁ kho dhuttā— “aḍḍhakāsī kira gaṇikā sāvatthiṁ gantukāmā”ti. Te magge pariyuṭṭhiṁsu. Assosi kho aḍḍhakāsī gaṇikā— “dhuttā kira magge pariyuṭṭhitā”ti. Bhagavato santike dūtaṁ pāhesi— “ahañhi upasampajjitukāmā; kathaṁ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabban”ti? Atha kho bhagavā etasmiṁ nidāne etasmiṁ pakaraṇe dhammiṁ kathaṁ katvā bhikkhū āmantesi—
20.e: At that time the courtesan Aḍḍhakāsī had gone forth with the nuns. She wanted to go to Sāvatthī to get the full ordination in the presence of the Buddha. Some scoundrels heard about this and besieged the road. When Aḍḍhakāsī heard about this, she sent a message to the Buddha, saying, “I want the full ordination. What should I do?” Soon afterwards the Buddha gave a teaching and addressed the monks:

20.s: “anujānāmi, bhikkhave, dūtenapi upasampādetun”ti.
20.e: “I allow you to give the full ordination also by messenger.”

20.s: Bhikkhudūtena upasampādenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: They ordained with a monk as messenger. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhudūtena upasampādetabbā. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
20.e: “You shouldn’t give the full ordination with a monk as messenger. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct.”

20.s: Sikkhamānadūtena upasampādenti …pe… sāmaṇeradūtena upasampādenti …pe… sāmaṇeridūtena upasampādenti …pe… bālāya abyattāya dūtena upasampādenti.
20.e: They ordained with a trainee nun as messenger … They ordained with a novice monk as messenger … They ordained with a novice nun as messenger … They ordained with an ignorant and incompetent nun as messenger.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bālāya abyattāya dūtena upasampādetabbā. Yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya dūtena upasampādetunti.
20.e: “You shouldn’t give the full ordination with an ignorant and incompetent nun as messenger. If you do, you commit an offense of wrong conduct. You should give the full ordination with a capable and competent nun as messenger.

20.s: Tāya dūtāya bhikkhuniyā saṅghaṁ upasaṅkamitvā ekaṁsaṁ uttarāsaṅgaṁ karitvā bhikkhūnaṁ pāde vanditvā ukkuṭikaṁ nisīditvā añjaliṁ paggahetvā evamassa vacanīyo—
20.e: That messenger nun should go to the Sangha, arrange her upper robe over one shoulder, bow down at the feet of the monks, squat on her heels, raise her joined palms, and say:

20.s: ‘itthannāmā, ayyā, itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Sā kenacideva antarāyena na āgacchati. Itthannāmā, ayyā, saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācati. Ullumpatu taṁ, ayyā, saṅgho anukampaṁ upādāya.
20.e: ‘Venerables, so-and-so is seeking the full ordination with venerable so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and has been fully ordained on one side in the Sangha of nuns. She hasn’t come because of an obstruction. She asks the Sangha for the full ordination. Please lift her up out of compassion.

20.s: Itthannāmā, ayyā, itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Sā kenacideva antarāyena na āgacchati. Dutiyampi, ayyā, itthannāmā saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācati. Ullumpatu taṁ, ayyā, saṅgho anukampaṁ upādāya.
20.e: Venerables, so-and-so is seeking the full ordination with venerable so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and has been fully ordained on one side in the Sangha of nuns. She hasn’t come because of an obstruction. For the second time, she asks the Sangha for the full ordination. Please lift her up out of compassion.

20.s: Itthannāmā, ayyā, itthannāmāya ayyāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Sā kenacideva antarāyena na āgacchati. Tatiyampi, ayyā, itthannāmā saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācati. Ullumpatu taṁ, ayyā, saṅgho anukampaṁ upādāyā’ti.
20.e: Venerables, so-and-so is seeking the full ordination with venerable so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and has been fully ordained on one side in the Sangha of nuns. She hasn’t come because of an obstruction. For the third time, she asks the Sangha for the full ordination. Please lift her up out of compassion.’

20.s: Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalena saṅgho ñāpetabbo—
20.e: A competent and capable monk should inform the Sangha:

20.s: ‘Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmā itthannāmāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Sā kenacideva antarāyena na āgacchati. Itthannāmā saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācati itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, saṅgho itthannāmaṁ upasampādeyya itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Esā ñatti.
20.e: ‘Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and has been fully ordained on one side in the Sangha of nuns. She is not present because of an obstruction. So-and-so is asking the Sangha for the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. If the Sangha is ready, it should give so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. This is the motion.

20.s: Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmā itthannāmāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Sā kenacideva antarāyena na āgacchati. Itthannāmā saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācati itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Saṅgho itthannāmaṁ upasampādeti itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmāya upasampadā itthannāmāya pavattiniyā, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.
20.e: Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and has been fully ordained on one side in the Sangha of nuns. She is not present because of an obstruction. So-and-so is asking the Sangha for the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. The Sangha gives so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. Any monk who approves of giving so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor should remain silent. Any monk who doesn’t approve should speak up.

20.s: Dutiyampi etamatthaṁ vadāmi …pe…
20.e: For the second time, I speak on this matter. Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and has been fully ordained on one side in the Sangha of nuns. She is not present because of an obstruction. So-and-so is asking the Sangha for the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. The Sangha gives so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. Any monk who approves of giving so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor should remain silent. Any monk who doesn’t approve should speak up.

20.s: tatiyampi etamatthaṁ vadāmi. Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Itthannāmā itthannāmāya upasampadāpekkhā. Ekatoupasampannā bhikkhunisaṅghe, visuddhā. Sā kenacideva antarāyena na āgacchati. Itthannāmā saṅghaṁ upasampadaṁ yācati itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Saṅgho itthannāmaṁ upasampādeti itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Yassāyasmato khamati itthannāmāya upasampadā itthannāmāya pavattiniyā, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.
20.e: For the third time, I speak on this matter. Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. So-and-so is seeking the full ordination with so-and-so. She is free from obstacles and has been fully ordained on one side in the Sangha of nuns. She is not present because of an obstruction. So-and-so is asking the Sangha for the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. The Sangha gives so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. Any monk who approves of giving so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor should remain silent. Any monk who doesn’t approve should speak up.

20.s: Upasampannā saṅghena itthannāmā itthannāmāya pavattiniyā. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmī’ti.
20.e: The Sangha has given so-and-so the full ordination with so-and-so as her mentor. The Sangha approves and is therefore silent. I will remember it thus.’

20.s: Tāvadeva chāyā metabbā, utuppamāṇaṁ ācikkhitabbaṁ, divasabhāgo ācikkhitabbo, saṅgīti ācikkhitabbā, bhikkhuniyo vattabbā— tassā tayo ca nissaye, aṭṭha ca akaraṇīyāni ācikkheyyāthā”ti.
20.e: Straightaway the time should be noted and the date should be pointed out. These should be declared jointly to everyone. The nuns should be told to point out the three supports and the eight things not to be done to the newly ordained nun.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo araññe viharanti. Dhuttā dūsenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ, ārocesuṁ.
20.e: At that time nuns were staying in the wilderness. Scoundrels raped them. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā araññe vatthabbaṁ. Yā vaseyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
20.e: “A nun shouldn’t stay in the wilderness. If she does, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarena upāsakena bhikkhunisaṅghassa uddosito dinno hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: On one occasion a lay follower gave a storehouse to the Sangha of nuns. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, uddositan”ti.
20.e: “I allow a storehouse.”

20.s: Uddosito na sammati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: The storehouse was too small. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, upassayan”ti.
20.e: “I allow a nunnery.”

20.s: Upassayo na sammati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: The nunnery was too small. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, navakamman”ti.
20.e: “I allow building work.”

20.s: Navakammaṁ na sammati. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: The building work was insufficient. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, puggalikampi kātun”ti.
20.e: “I allow you to build for individuals.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā itthī sannisinnagabbhā bhikkhunīsu pabbajitā hoti. Tassā pabbajitāya gabbho vuṭṭhāti. Atha kho tassā bhikkhuniyā etadahosi— “kathaṁ nu kho mayā imasmiṁ dārake paṭipajjitabban”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: At one time a pregnant woman went forth as a nun. After giving birth, she asked the nuns what to do with the baby boy. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, posetuṁ, yāva so dārako viññutaṁ pāpuṇātī”ti.
20.e: “I allow you to rear him until he becomes self-reliant.”

20.s: Atha kho tassā bhikkhuniyā etadahosi— “mayā ca na labbhā ekikāya vatthuṁ, aññāya ca bhikkhuniyā na labbhā dārakena saha vatthuṁ, kathaṁ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabban”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: That nun thought, “I’m not allowed to stay by myself and other nuns are not allowed to stay with a male child. What should I do now?” They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekaṁ bhikkhuniṁ sammannitvā tassā bhikkhuniyā dutiyaṁ dātuṁ.
20.e: “The nuns should appoint a nun as her companion.

20.s: Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbā. Paṭhamaṁ bhikkhunī yācitabbā, yācitvā byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo—
20.e: And she should be appointed like this. First a nun should be asked, and then a capable and competent nun should inform the Sangha:

20.s: ‘Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, saṅgho itthannāmaṁ bhikkhuniṁ sammanneyya itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyaṁ. Esā ñatti.
20.e: ‘Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. If the Sangha is ready, it should appoint nun so-and-so as a companion to nun so-and-so. This is the motion.

20.s: Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṁ bhikkhuniṁ sammannati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyaṁ. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā sammuti itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyāya, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.
20.e: Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. The Sangha appoints nun so-and-so as a companion to nun so-and-so. Any nun who approves of appointing nun so-and-so as a companion to nun so-and-so should remain silent. Any nun who doesn’t approve should speak up.

20.s: Sammatā saṅghena itthannāmā bhikkhunī itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyā. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmī’”ti.
20.e: The Sangha has appointed nun so-and-so as a companion to nun so-and-so. The Sangha approves and is therefore silent. I will remember it thus.’”

20.s: Atha kho tassā dutiyikāya bhikkhuniyā etadahosi— “kathaṁ nu kho mayā imasmiṁ dārake paṭipajjitabban”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: That companion nun thought, “How should I act in regard to this boy?” They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ṭhapetvā sāgāraṁ yathā aññasmiṁ purise paṭipajjanti evaṁ tasmiṁ dārake paṭipajjitun”ti.
20.e: “Apart from staying in the same dwelling, the companion nun should act toward him as she would toward any other male.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī garudhammaṁ ajjhāpannā hoti mānattacārinī. Atha kho tassā bhikkhuniyā etadahosi— “mayā ca na labbhā ekikāya vatthuṁ, aññāya ca bhikkhuniyā na labbhā saha mayā vatthuṁ, kathaṁ nu kho mayā paṭipajjitabban”ti? Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: On one occasion a nun who had committed a heavy offense was undertaking the trial period. She thought, “I’m not allowed to stay by myself and other nuns are not allowed to stay with me. What should I do now?” They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, ekaṁ bhikkhuniṁ sammannitvā tassā bhikkhuniyā dutiyaṁ dātuṁ.
20.e: “You should appoint a nun as her companion.

20.s: Evañca pana, bhikkhave, sammannitabbā. Paṭhamaṁ bhikkhunī yācitabbā, yācitvā byattāya bhikkhuniyā paṭibalāya saṅgho ñāpetabbo—
20.e: And she should be appointed like this. First a nun should be asked, and then a capable and competent nun should inform the Sangha:

20.s: ‘Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, saṅgho itthannāmaṁ bhikkhuniṁ sammanneyya itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyaṁ. Esā ñatti.
20.e: ‘Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. If the Sangha is ready, it should appoint nun so-and-so as a companion to nun so-and-so. This is the motion.

20.s: Suṇātu me, ayye, saṅgho. Saṅgho itthannāmaṁ bhikkhuniṁ sammannati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyaṁ. Yassā ayyāya khamati itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā sammuti itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyāya, sā tuṇhassa; yassā nakkhamati, sā bhāseyya.
20.e: Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. The Sangha appoints nun so-and-so as a companion to nun so-and-so. Any nun who approves of appointing nun so-and-so as a companion to nun so-and-so should remain silent. Any nun who doesn’t approve should speak up.

20.s: Sammatā saṅghena itthannāmā bhikkhunī itthannāmāya bhikkhuniyā dutiyā. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmī’”ti.
20.e: The Sangha has appointed nun so-and-so as a companion to nun so-and-so. The Sangha approves and is therefore silent. I will remember it thus.’”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya vibbhami. Sā puna paccāgantvā bhikkhuniyo upasampadaṁ yāci. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: On one occasion a nun verbally renounced the training and disrobed. Later she returned and asked the nuns for the full ordination. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā sikkhāpaccakkhānaṁ; yadeva sā vibbhantā tadeva sā abhikkhunī”ti.
20.e: “A nun can’t verbally renounce the training. When she disrobes, she is no longer a nun.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī sakāvāsā titthāyatanaṁ saṅkami. Sā puna paccāgantvā bhikkhuniyo upasampadaṁ yāci. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: On one occasion a nun joined another religious community while still wearing her robes. Later she returned and asked the nuns for the full ordination. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Yā sā, bhikkhave, bhikkhunī sakāvāsā titthāyatanaṁ saṅkantā, sā āgatā na upasampādetabbā”ti.
20.e: “If a nun goes over to another religious community while still wearing her robes and then returns, she shouldn’t be given the full ordination again.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo purisehi abhivādanaṁ, kesacchedanaṁ, nakhacchedanaṁ, vaṇappaṭikammaṁ, kukkuccāyantā na sādiyanti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: At that time the nuns, being afraid of wrongdoing, did not consent to men bowing down to them, or to men shaving their heads, cutting their nails, or treating their sores. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, sāditun”ti.
20.e: “I allow you to consent to these things.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo pallaṅkena nisīdanti paṇhisamphassaṁ sādiyantī. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: At that time the nuns were sitting cross-legged, enjoying the touch of their heels. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā pallaṅkena nisīditabbaṁ. Yā nisīdeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
20.e: “A nun shouldn’t sit cross-legged. If she does, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena aññatarā bhikkhunī gilānā hoti. Tassā vinā pallaṅkena na phāsu hoti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: On one occasion there was a sick nun who was not comfortable without sitting cross-legged. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā aḍḍhapallaṅkan”ti.
20.e: “I allow a nun to sit half-cross-legged.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo vaccakuṭiyā vaccaṁ karonti. Chabbaggiyā bhikkhuniyo tattheva gabbhaṁ pātenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: At that time the nuns were using a restroom for defecating. And the nuns from the group of six performed abortions there. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā vaccakuṭiyā vacco kātabbo. Yā kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, heṭṭhā vivaṭe uparipaṭicchanne vaccaṁ kātun”ti.
20.e: “A nun shouldn’t defecate in a restroom. If she does, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow the nuns to defecate in a place that’s open underneath but concealed on top.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo cuṇṇena nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti …pe… seyyathāpi gihinī kāmabhoginiyo”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: At that time the nuns were bathing with bath powder. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!” They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā cuṇṇena nahāyitabbaṁ. Yā nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, kukkusaṁ mattikan”ti.
20.e: “A nun shouldn’t bathe with bath powder. If she does, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow bran and clay.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo vāsitakāya mattikāya nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti …pe… seyyathāpi gihinī kāmabhoginiyo”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: At that time the nuns were bathing with scented clay. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!” They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā vāsitakāya mattikāya nahāyitabbaṁ. Yā nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, pakatimattikan”ti.
20.e: “A nun shouldn’t bathe with scented clay. If she does, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. I allow ordinary clay.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo jantāghare nahāyantiyo kolāhalaṁ akaṁsu. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: On one occasion when the nuns were bathing in a sauna, they made a racket. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā jantāghare nahāyitabbaṁ. Yā nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
20.e: “A nun shouldn’t bathe in a sauna. If she does, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo paṭisote nahāyanti dhārāsamphassaṁ sādiyantī. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: On one occasion the nuns were bathing against the stream, enjoying the touch of the current. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā paṭisote nahāyitabbaṁ. Yā nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
20.e: “A nun shouldn’t bathe against the stream. If she does, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo atitthe nahāyanti. Dhuttā dūsenti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: On one occasion the nuns bathed away from a ford. Scoundrels raped them. They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā atitthe nahāyitabbaṁ. Yā nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti.
20.e: “A nun shouldn’t bathe away from a ford. If she does, she commits an offense of wrong conduct.”

20.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhikkhuniyo purisatitthe nahāyanti. Manussā ujjhāyanti khiyyanti vipācenti …pe… seyyathāpi gihinī kāmabhoginiyo”ti. Bhagavato etamatthaṁ ārocesuṁ.
20.e: On one occasion the nuns bathed at a ford for men. People complained and criticized them, “They’re just like householders who indulge in worldly pleasures!” They told the Buddha.

20.s: “Na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā purisatitthe nahāyitabbaṁ. Yā nahāyeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassa. Anujānāmi, bhikkhave, mahilātitthe nahāyitun”ti.
20.e: “A nun shouldn’t bathe at a ford for men. If she does, she commits an offense of wrong conduct. A nun should bathe at a ford for women.”

20.s:
Rajokiṇṇena koṭṭhake,
ānandassa pavedayi;
Bhabboti nayato yāci,
mātāti posikāti ca.
20.e:
At the gatehouse covered in dust,
Declared to Ānanda;
He asked wisely about capability,
About mother and upbringing.

20.s:
Vassasataṁ tadahu ca,
abhikkhupaccāsīsanā;
Pavāraṇā garudhammā,
dve vassā anakkosanā.
20.e:
One hundred years and that very day,
Without monks, seeking;
Invitation, heavy offense,
Two years, not abusing.

20.s:
Ovaṭo ca aṭṭha dhammā,
yāvajīvānuvattanā;
Garudhammapaṭiggāho,
sāvassā upasampadā.
20.e:
And may not, eight principles,
Practicing all one’s life;
Receiving the important principles,
That was her ordination.

20.s:
Vassasahassaṁ pañceva,
kumbhathenakasetaṭṭi;
Mañjiṭṭhikaupamāhi,
evaṁ saddhammahiṁsanā.
20.e:
A thousand years, just five,
Thieves, whiteheads;
Red rot, with similes,
Thus the true Teaching was injured.

20.s:
Āḷiṁ bandheyya pāeva,
puna saddhammasaṇṭhiti;
Upasampādetuṁ ayyā,
yathāvuḍḍhābhivādanā.
20.e:
Not to mention he would make a dyke,
Again he stabilized the true Teaching;
To ordain, venerable,
Bow down according to seniority.

20.s:
Na karissanti kimeva,
sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇaṁ;
Ovādaṁ pātimokkhañca,
kena nu kho upassayaṁ.
20.e:
They will not, how then,
Common, not in common;
Instruction, and Monastic Code,
Who, nunnery.

20.s:
Na jānanti ca ācikkhi,
na karonti ca bhikkhuhi;
Paṭiggahetuṁ bhikkhūhi,
bhikkhunīhi paṭiggaho.
20.e:
And they do not know, he told,
And did not do, with monks;
To receive by monks,
Receiving by nuns.

20.s:
Ācikkhi kammaṁ bhikkhūhi,
ujjhāyanti bhikkhunīhi vā;
Ācikkhituṁ bhaṇḍanañca,
ropetvā uppalāya ca.
20.e:
He told, procedure by monks,
They complained, or with nuns;
To tell, and arguing,
Having determined, and with Uppalā.

20.s:
Sāvatthiyā kaddamoda,
avandi kāya ūru ca;
Aṅgajātañca obhāsaṁ,
sampayojenti vaggikā.
20.e:
At Sāvatthī, muddy water,
Non-respect, body, and thigh;
And genitals, indecent speech,
The group associated inappropriately.

20.s:
Avandiyo daṇḍakammaṁ,
bhikkhuniyo tathā puna;
Āvaraṇañca ovādaṁ,
kappati nu kho pakkami.
20.e:
Non-respect, penalty,
So again the nuns;
And restriction, instruction,
Is it allowable, he set out wandering.

20.s:
Bālā vatthuvinicchayā,
ovādaṁ saṅgho pañcahi;
Duve tisso na gaṇhanti,
bālā gilānagamikaṁ.
20.e:
Ignorant, reason, investigation,
Instruction, Sangha, with five;
Two or three, they did not agree,
Ignorant ones, sick, departing.

20.s:
Aṭṭhillaṁ gohanukena,
hatthakocchaṁ pādaṁ tathā;
Ūruṁ mukhaṁ dantamaṁsaṁ,
ālimpomaddacuṇṇanā.
20.e:
Bone, cow’s jaw bone,
Hand, back of hand, so foot;
Thigh, face, gums,
Ointment, applied creams, powdered.

20.s:
Lañchenti aṅgarāgañca,
mukharāgaṁ tathā duve;
Avaṅgaṁ visesoloko,
sālokena naccena ca.
20.e:
They applied, body cosmetics,
Facial cosmetics, so both;
Eye cosmetics, facial mark, staring,
With exposed to view, and with dancing.

20.s:
Vesī pānāgāraṁ sūnaṁ,
āpaṇaṁ vaḍḍhi vaṇijjā;
Dāsaṁ dāsiṁ kammakaraṁ,
kammakāriṁ upaṭṭhayyuṁ.
20.e:
Sex worker, bar, slaughterhouse,
Shop, loan, trade;
Male and female slaves, male servants,
Female servants, they would attend on.

20.s:
Tiracchānaharītaki,
sandhārayanti namatakaṁ;
Nīlaṁ pītaṁ lohitakaṁ,
mañjiṭṭhakaṇhacīvarā.
20.e:
Animals, greens,
They wore felt;
Blue, yellow, red,
Magenta, and black robes.

20.s:
Mahāraṅgamahānāma-
acchinnā dīghameva ca;
Pupphaphalakañcukañca,
tirīṭakañca dhārayuṁ.
20.e:
Orange and beige,
Single piece, and just long;
Floral, fruit, and close-fitting jacket,
And lodh tree, they wore.

20.s:
Bhikkhunī sikkhamānāya,
sāmaṇerāya accaye;
Niyyādite parikkhāre,
bhikkhuniyova issarā.
20.e:
Nun, of a trainee nun,
Of a novice nun, after death;
The requisites are handed back,
Just the nuns are the owners.

20.s:
Bhikkhussa sāmaṇerassa,
upāsakassupāsikā;
Aññesañca parikkhāre,
niyyāte bhikkhuissarā.
20.e:
Of a monk, of a novice monk,
Of a lay follower, a female lay follower;
And the requisites of others,
It should be handed back, the monks are the owners.

20.s:
Mallī gabbhaṁ pattamūlaṁ,
byañjanaṁ āmisena ca;
Ussannañca bāḷhataraṁ,
sannidhikatamāmisaṁ.
20.e:
Female wrestler, fetus, the bottom of the bowl,
Genitals, and with requisite;
Abundance, greater,
Stored up requisites.

20.s:
Bhikkhūnaṁ yādisaṁ bhoṭṭhaṁ,
Bhikkhunīnaṁ tathā kare;
Senāsanaṁ utuniyo,
Makkhīyati paṭāṇi ca.
20.e:
As above for the monks,
So it should be done for the nuns;
Dwelling, menstruating,
It was stained, and menstruation pads.

20.s:
Chijjanti sabbakālañca,
animittāpi dissare;
Nimittā lohitā ceva,
tatheva dhuvalohitā.
20.e:
They snapped, and all the times,
Also those without genitals were seen;
Genitals, and just blood,
Just so continuous blood.

20.s:
Dhuvacoḷapaggharantī,
sikharaṇitthipaṇḍakā;
Vepurisī ca sambhinnā,
ubhatobyañjanāpi ca.
20.e:
Continuous pad, incontinent,
Prolapse, without sexual organs;
And manlike, fistula,
And also gynandromorph.

20.s:
Animittādito katvā,
yāva ubhatobyañjanā;
Etaṁ peyyālato heṭṭhā,
kuṭṭhaṁ gaṇḍo kilāso ca.
20.e:
Having set out without genitals etc.,
As far as gynandromorph;
This is according to the repetition above,
Leprosy, abscesses, and mild leprosy.

20.s:
Sosāpamāro mānusī,
itthīsi bhujissāsi ca;
Aṇaṇā na rājabhaṭī,
anuññātā ca vīsati.
20.e:
Tuberculosis and epilepsy, are you human,
Are you a woman, and are you free;
Debtless, not employed by the king,
And permitted, twenty.

20.s:
Paripuṇṇā ca kiṁnāmā,
kānāmā te pavattinī;
Catuvīsantarāyānaṁ,
pucchitvā upasampadā.
20.e:
And full set, what name,
What is the name of your mentor;
Of the twenty-four obstacles,
Having asked, ordination.

20.s:
Vitthāyanti ananusiṭṭhā,
saṅghamajjhe tatheva ca;
Upajjhāgāha saṅghāṭi,
uttarantaravāsako.
20.e:
They were embarrassed, not instructed,
And just so in the midst of the Sangha;
Choosing a preceptor, outer robe,
Upper robe, sarong.

20.s:
Saṅkaccudakasāṭi ca,
ācikkhitvāna pesaye;
Bālā asammatekato,
yāce pucchantarāyikā.
20.e:
Chest wrap, and bathing robe,
Having pointed out, should send away;
Ignorant ones, not appointed,
She should ask, interval on asking.

20.s:
Ekatoupasampannā,
bhikkhusaṅghe tathā puna;
Chāyā utu divasā ca,
saṅgīti tayo nissaye.
20.e:
Ordained on one side,
Again so with the Sangha of monks;
Time, season, and date,
Jointly, three supports.

20.s:
Aṭṭha akaraṇīyāni,
kālaṁ sabbattha aṭṭheva;
Na pavārenti bhikkhunī,
bhikkhusaṅghaṁ tatheva ca.
20.e:
Eight things not to be done,
The right time, everywhere, just eight;
The nuns did not invite,
And just so the Sangha of monks.

20.s:
Kolāhalaṁ purebhattaṁ,
vikāle ca kolāhalaṁ;
Uposathaṁ pavāraṇaṁ,
savacanīyānuvādanaṁ.
20.e:
Racket, before the meal,
And too late, racket;
Observance-day ceremony, invitation ceremony,
Direction, instruction.

20.s:
Okāsaṁ code sārenti,
paṭikkhittaṁ mahesinā;
Tatheva bhikkhu bhikkhunī,
anuññātaṁ mahesinā.
20.e:
Permission, accused, they reminded,
Was prohibited by the Great Sage;
In that way a monk to a nun,
Was allowed by the Great Sage.

20.s:
Yānaṁ gilānayuttañca,
yānugghātaḍḍhakāsikā;
Bhikkhu sikkhā sāmaṇera,
sāmaṇerī ca bālāya.
20.e:
Vehicle, sick, and pulled,
Jolted around in a vehicle, Aḍḍhakāsī;
Monk, trainee nun, novice monk,
And novice nun, with an ignorant one.

20.s:
Araññe upāsakena,
uddosito upassayaṁ;
Na sammati navakammaṁ,
nisinnagabbhaekikā.
20.e:
In the wilderness, with a lay follower,
Storehouse, nunnery;
Not sufficient, building work,
Pregnant, by herself.

20.s:
Sāgārañca garudhammaṁ,
paccakkhāya ca saṅkami;
Abhivādanakesā ca,
nakhā ca vaṇakammanā.
20.e:
And the same building, heavy offense,
And verbally renounced, joined;
And bowing down, and hair,
And nails, treating sores.

20.s:
Pallaṅkena gilānā ca,
vaccaṁ cuṇṇena vāsitaṁ;
Jantāghare paṭisote,
atitthe purisena ca.
20.e:
Cross-legged, and sick,
Feces, with bath powder, scented;
In a sauna, against the stream,
Away from a ford, and with men.

20.s:
Mahāgotamī āyāci,
ānando cāpi yoniso;
Parisā catasso honti,
pabbajjā jinasāsane.
20.e:
Mahāgotamī asked,
And so did Ānanda wisely;
There are four assemblies,
Going forth in the instruction of the Victor.

20.s:
Saṁvegajananatthāya,
saddhammassa ca vuddhiyā;
Āturassāva bhesajjaṁ,
evaṁ buddhena desitaṁ.
20.e:
For the purpose of seeing the urgency,
And for the purpose of growth in the true Teaching;
Like medicine for the sick,
So it was taught by the Buddha.

20.s:
Evaṁ vinītā saddhamme,
mātugāmāpi itarā;
Yāyanti accutaṁ ṭhānaṁ,
yattha gantvā na socareti.
20.e:
Thus trained in the true Teaching,
Other women too;
They go to where there is no death,
Having gone there, they do not sorrow.”

21.s: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo bhikkhū āmantesi— “ekamidāhaṁ, āvuso, samayaṁ pāvāya kusināraṁ addhānamaggappaṭipanno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi. Atha khvāhaṁ, āvuso, maggā okkamma aññatarasmiṁ rukkhamūle nisīdiṁ.
21.e: Then Venerable Mahākassapa addressed the monks: “On one occasion, as I was traveling from Pāvā to Kusināra with a large sangha of five hundred monks, I left the road and sat down at the foot of a tree.
21.t: The chapter on the first council (21. Pañcasatikakkhandhaka) — 1. The origin story of the communal recitation (1. Saṅgītinidāna)

21.s: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro ājīvako kusinārāya mandāravapupphaṁ gahetvā pāvaṁ addhānamaggappaṭipanno hoti. Addasaṁ kho ahaṁ, āvuso, taṁ ājīvakaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ. Disvāna taṁ ājīvakaṁ etadavocaṁ— ‘apāvuso, amhākaṁ satthāraṁ jānāsī’ti?
21.e: Just then a follower of the Ājīvakas was traveling toward Pāvā on the same road, holding a coral-tree flower that he had picked up in Kusināra. When I saw him coming, I asked him, ‘Do you know anything about our Teacher?’

21.s: ‘Āmāvuso, jānāmi. Ajja sattāhaparinibbuto samaṇo gotamo. Tato me idaṁ mandāravapupphaṁ gahitan’ti.
21.e: ‘I do. Today it’s seven days since the ascetic Gotama attained final extinguishment. That’s why I carry this coral-tree flower.’

21.s: Tatrāvuso, ye te bhikkhū avītarāgā appekacce bāhā paggayha kandanti, chinnapātaṁ papatanti, āvaṭṭanti, vivaṭṭanti— atikhippaṁ bhagavā parinibbuto, atikhippaṁ sugato parinibbuto, atikhippaṁ cakkhuṁ loke antarahitanti. Ye pana te bhikkhū vītarāgā te satā sampajānā adhivāsenti— aniccā saṅkhārā, taṁ kutettha labbhāti.
21.e: Some of the monks there who were not yet free from desire threw up their arms and cried, collapsed on the ground, and rolled back and forth, lamenting, ‘The Buddha, the Happy One, has attained final extinguishment too soon—too soon has the eye of the world been put out!’ But the monks there who were free from desire bore it with mindfulness and full awareness, saying, ‘All phenomena are impermanent. How could it be any different?’

21.s: Atha khvāhaṁ, āvuso, te bhikkhū etadavocaṁ— ‘alaṁ, āvuso, mā socittha; mā paridevittha. Nanvetaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā paṭikacceva akkhātaṁ— sabbeheva piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo aññathābhāvo. Taṁ kutettha āvuso labbhā, yaṁ taṁ jātaṁ bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ palokadhammaṁ, taṁ vata mā palujjīti— netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjatī’ti.
21.e: I said, ‘Please stop grieving, stop lamenting. Didn’t the Buddha warn us that we must be separated from everyone and everything dear and agreeable to us? How could that which is born, become, made up, and of a nature to fall apart, not fall apart? That’s impossible.’

21.s: Tena kho panāvuso, samayena subhaddo nāma vuḍḍhapabbajito tassaṁ parisāyaṁ nisinno hoti. Atha kho, āvuso, subhaddo vuḍḍhapabbajito te bhikkhū etadavoca— ‘alaṁ, āvuso, mā socittha; mā paridevittha. Sumuttā mayaṁ tena mahāsamaṇena; upaddutā ca mayaṁ homa— idaṁ vo kappati, idaṁ vo na kappatīti. Idāni pana mayaṁ yaṁ icchissāma taṁ karissāma, yaṁ na icchissāma na taṁ karissāmā’ti.
21.e: On that occasion a monk called Subhadda, who had gone forth when old, was part of that group. He said to the monks, ‘Please stop grieving, stop lamenting. It’s good that we are free from that great ascetic. We were oppressed, always being told what’s allowable and what’s not. Now we can do what we like and not do what we don’t like.’

21.s: Handa mayaṁ, āvuso, dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyāma. Pure adhammo dippati, dhammo paṭibāhiyyati; pure avinayo dippati vinayo paṭibāhiyyati; pure adhammavādino balavanto honti, dhammavādino dubbalā honti; pure avinayavādino balavanto honti, vinayavādino dubbalā hontī”ti.
21.e: So then, let’s recite the Teaching and the Monastic Law— before what’s contrary to the Teaching shines forth and the Teaching is obstructed; before what’s contrary to the Monastic Law shines forth and the Monastic Law is obstructed; before those who speak contrary to the Teaching become strong and those who speak in accordance with it become weak; before those who speak contrary to the Monastic Law become strong and those who speak in accordance with it become weak.”

21.s: “Tena hi, bhante, thero bhikkhū uccinatū”ti. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo ekenūnapañcaarahantasatāni uccini. Bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ mahākassapaṁ etadavocuṁ— “ayaṁ, bhante, āyasmā ānando kiñcāpi sekkho, abhabbo chandā dosā mohā bhayā agatiṁ gantuṁ. Bahu ca anena bhagavato santike dhammo ca vinayo ca pariyatto. Tena hi, bhante, thero āyasmantampi ānandaṁ uccinatū”ti. Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantampi ānandaṁ uccini.
21.e: “Well then, venerable, please select the monks.” Mahākassapa then selected four hundred and ninety-nine perfected ones. The monks said to him, “There’s Venerable Ānanda who, although still a trainee, is incapable of acting out of desire, ill will, confusion, or fear. He has learned many teachings and much Monastic Law from the Buddha. Please invite him as well.” And he did.

21.s: Atha kho therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ etadahosi— “kattha nu kho mayaṁ dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyeyyāmā”ti? Atha kho therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ etadahosi— “rājagahaṁ kho mahāgocaraṁ pahūtasenāsanaṁ, yannūna mayaṁ rājagahe vassaṁ vasantā dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyeyyāma. Na aññe bhikkhū rājagahe vassaṁ upagaccheyyun”ti.
21.e: The senior monks thought, “Where should we recite the Teaching and the Monastic Law?” It occurred to them, “Rājagaha has much almsfood and many dwellings. Let’s spend the rainy season there in order to recite the Teaching and the Monastic Law. No other monks should enter the rainy-season residence at Rājagaha.”

21.s: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo saṅghaṁ ñāpesi—
21.e: And Venerable Mahākassapa informed the Sangha:

21.s: “Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, saṅgho imāni pañca bhikkhusatāni sammanneyya— rājagahe vassaṁ vasantāni dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyituṁ, na aññehi bhikkhūhi rājagahe vassaṁ vasitabbanti. Esā ñatti.
21.e: “Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. If the Sangha is ready, it should appoint these five hundred monks to spend the rainy season at Rājagaha in order to recite the Teaching and the Monastic Law. No other monks should spend the rainy-season residence at Rājagaha. This is the motion.

21.s: Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho. Imāni pañca bhikkhusatāni sammannati— rājagahe vassaṁ vasantāni dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyituṁ, na aññehi bhikkhūhi rājagahe vassaṁ vasitabbanti. Yassāyasmato khamati imesaṁ pañcannaṁ bhikkhusatānaṁ sammuti— rājagahe vassaṁ vasantānaṁ dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyituṁ, na aññehi bhikkhūhi rājagahe vassaṁ vasitabbanti— so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.
21.e: Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. The Sangha appoints these five hundred monks to spend the rainy season at Rājagaha in order to recite the Teaching and the Monastic Law. No other monks should spend the rainy-season residence at Rājagaha. Any monk who approves of appointing these five hundred monks to spend the rainy season at Rājagaha in order to recite the Teaching and the Monastic Law, with no other monks spending the rainy-season residence at Rājagaha, should remain silent. Any monk who doesn’t approve should speak up.

21.s: Sammatāni saṅghena imāni pañca bhikkhusatāni rājagahe vassaṁ vasantāni dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyituṁ, na aññehi bhikkhūhi rājagahe vassaṁ vasitabbanti. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmī”ti.
21.e: The Sangha has appointed these five hundred monks to spend the rainy season at Rājagaha in order to recite the Teaching and the Monastic Law. No other monks should spend the rainy-season residence at Rājagaha. The Sangha approves and is therefore silent. I will remember it thus.”

21.s: Atha kho therā bhikkhū rājagahaṁ agamaṁsu dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyituṁ. Atha kho therānaṁ bhikkhūnaṁ etadahosi— “bhagavatā kho, āvuso, khaṇḍaphullapaṭisaṅkharaṇaṁ vaṇṇitaṁ. Handa mayaṁ, āvuso, paṭhamaṁ māsaṁ khaṇḍaphullaṁ paṭisaṅkharoma; majjhimaṁ māsaṁ sannipatitvā dhammañca vinayañca saṅgāyissāmā”ti.
21.e: The senior monks then went to Rājagaha to recite the Teaching and the Monastic Law. They thought, “The Buddha has praised repairing what’s defective and broken. Well then, let’s spend the first month doing repairs, and then gather for the middle month to recite the Teaching and the Monastic Law.”

21.s: Atha kho therā bhikkhū paṭhamaṁ māsaṁ khaṇḍaphullaṁ paṭisaṅkhariṁsu. Atha kho āyasmā ānando— “sve sannipāto na kho metaṁ patirūpaṁ, yohaṁ sekkho samāno sannipātaṁ gaccheyyan”ti— bahudeva rattiṁ kāyagatāya satiyā vītināmetvā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ “nipajjissāmī”ti kāyaṁ āvajjesi. Appattañca sīsaṁ bibbohanaṁ, bhūmito ca pādā muttā. Etasmiṁ antare anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimucci. Atha kho āyasmā ānando arahā samāno sannipātaṁ agamāsi.
21.e: They then spent the first month doing repairs. Venerable Ānanda thought, “It wouldn’t be proper for me to go to the assembly tomorrow if I’m still a trainee.” After spending most of the night with mindfulness directed to the body, early in the morning he bent over to lie down. In the interval between his feet coming off the ground and his head hitting the pillow, his mind was freed from the corruptions through letting go. And Venerable Ānanda went to the assembly as a perfected one.

21.s: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo saṅghaṁ ñāpesi—
21.e: Venerable Mahākassapa then informed the Sangha:

21.s: “Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, ahaṁ upāliṁ vinayaṁ puccheyyan”ti.
21.e: “Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. If the Sangha is ready, I will ask Upāli about the Monastic Law.”

21.s: Āyasmā upāli saṅghaṁ ñāpesi—
21.e: Venerable Upāli informed the Sangha:

21.s: “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, ahaṁ āyasmatā mahākassapena vinayaṁ puṭṭho vissajjeyyan”ti.
21.e: “Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. If the Sangha is ready, I will reply when asked by Venerable Mahākassapa about the Monastic Law.”

21.s: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṁ upāliṁ etadavoca— “paṭhamaṁ, āvuso upāli, pārājikaṁ kattha paññattan”ti?
21.e: Mahākassapa then asked Upāli, “Where was the first offense entailing expulsion laid down?”

21.s: “Vesāliyaṁ, bhante”ti.
21.e: “At Vesālī.”

21.s: “Kaṁ ārabbhā”ti?
21.e: “Who is it about?”

21.s: “Sudinnaṁ kalandaputtaṁ ārabbhā”ti.
21.e: “Sudinna the Kalandian.”

21.s: “Kismiṁ vatthusmin”ti?
21.e: “What is it about?”

21.s: “Methunadhamme”ti.
21.e: “Sexual intercourse.”

21.s: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṁ upāliṁ paṭhamassa pārājikassa vatthumpi pucchi, nidānampi pucchi, puggalampi pucchi, paññattimpi pucchi, anupaññattimpi pucchi, āpattimpi pucchi, anāpattimpi pucchi.
21.e: Mahākassapa also asked Upāli about the topic of the first offense entailing expulsion, about the origin story, about the person, about the rule, about the additions to the rule, about the offense, and about the non-offenses.

21.s: “Dutiyaṁ panāvuso upāli, pārājikaṁ kattha paññattan”ti?
21.e: “And where was the second offense entailing expulsion laid down?”

21.s: “Rājagahe, bhante”ti.
21.e: “At Rājagaha.”

21.s: “Kaṁ ārabbhā”ti?
21.e: “Who is it about?”

21.s: “Dhaniyaṁ kumbhakāraputtaṁ ārabbhā”ti.
21.e: “Dhaniya the potter.”

21.s: “Kismiṁ vatthusmin”ti?
21.e: “What is it about?”

21.s: “Adinnādāne”ti.
21.e: “Stealing.”

21.s: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṁ upāliṁ dutiyassa pārājikassa vatthumpi pucchi, nidānampi pucchi, puggalampi pucchi, paññattimpi pucchi, anupaññattimpi pucchi, āpattimpi pucchi, anāpattimpi pucchi.
21.e: Mahākassapa also asked Upāli about the topic of the second offense entailing expulsion, about the origin story, about the person, about the rule, about the additions to the rule, about the offense, and about the non-offenses.

21.s: “Tatiyaṁ panāvuso upāli, pārājikaṁ kattha paññattan”ti?
21.e: “And where was the third offense entailing expulsion laid down?”

21.s: “Vesāliyaṁ, bhante”ti.
21.e: “At Vesālī.”

21.s: “Kaṁ ārabbhā”ti?
21.e: “Who is it about?”

21.s: “Sambahule bhikkhū ārabbhā”ti.
21.e: “A number of monks.”

21.s: “Kismiṁ vatthusmin”ti?
21.e: “What is it about?”

21.s: “Manussaviggahe”ti.
21.e: “Human beings.”

21.s: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṁ upāliṁ tatiyassa pārājikassa vatthumpi pucchi, nidānampi pucchi, puggalampi pucchi, paññattimpi pucchi, anupaññattimpi pucchi, āpattimpi pucchi, anāpattimpi pucchi.
21.e: Mahākassapa also asked Upāli about the topic of the third offense entailing expulsion, about the origin story, about the person, about the rule, about the additions to the rule, about the offense, and about the non-offenses.

21.s: “Catutthaṁ panāvuso upāli, pārājikaṁ kattha paññattan”ti?
21.e: “And where was the fourth offense entailing expulsion laid down?”

21.s: “Vesāliyaṁ, bhante”ti.
21.e: “At Vesālī.”

21.s: “Kaṁ ārabbhā”ti?
21.e: “Who is it about?”

21.s: “Vaggumudātīriye bhikkhū ārabbhā”ti.
21.e: “The monks from the banks of the Vaggumudā.”

21.s: “Kismiṁ vatthusmin”ti?
21.e: “What is it about?”

21.s: “Uttarimanussadhamme”ti.
21.e: “Superhuman qualities.”

21.s: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṁ upāliṁ catutthassa pārājikassa vatthumpi pucchi, nidānampi pucchi, puggalampi pucchi, paññattimpi pucchi, anupaññattimpi pucchi, āpattimpi pucchi, anāpattimpi pucchi.
21.e: Mahākassapa also asked Upāli about the topic of the fourth offense entailing expulsion, about the origin story, about the person, about the rule, about the additions to the rule, about the offense, and about the non-offenses.

21.s: Eteneva upāyena ubhatovibhaṅge pucchi. Puṭṭho puṭṭho āyasmā upāli vissajjesi.
21.e: In this way he asked about the analyses of both Monastic Codes. Upāli was able to reply to each and every question.

21.s: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo saṅghaṁ ñāpesi—
21.e: Venerable Mahākassapa then informed the Sangha:

21.s: “Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, ahaṁ ānandaṁ dhammaṁ puccheyyan”ti.
21.e: “Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. If the Sangha is ready, I will ask Ānanda about the Teaching.”

21.s: Āyasmā ānando saṅghaṁ ñāpesi—
21.e: Venerable Ānanda informed the Sangha:

21.s: “Suṇātu me, bhante, saṅgho. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, ahaṁ āyasmatā mahākassapena dhammaṁ puṭṭho vissajjeyyan”ti.
21.e: “Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. If the Sangha is ready, I will reply when asked by Venerable Mahākassapa about the Teaching.”

21.s: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca— “brahmajālaṁ, āvuso ānanda, kattha bhāsitan”ti?
21.e: Mahākassapa then asked Ānanda, “Where was ‘The Supreme Net’ spoken?”

21.s: “Antarā ca, bhante, rājagahaṁ antarā ca nāḷandaṁ rājāgārake ambalaṭṭhikāyā”ti.
21.e: “At the royal rest-house at Ambalaṭṭhikā, between Rājagaha and Nāḷanda.”

21.s: “Kaṁ ārabbhā”ti?
21.e: “Who is it about?”

21.s: “Suppiyañca paribbājakaṁ brahmadattañca māṇavan”ti.
21.e: “The wanderer Suppiya and the young brahmin Brahmadatta.”

21.s: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ brahmajālassa nidānampi pucchi, puggalampi pucchi.
21.e: Mahākassapa also asked Ānanda about the origin story of ‘The Supreme Net’ and about the person.

21.s: “Sāmaññaphalaṁ panāvuso ānanda, kattha bhāsitan”ti?
21.e: “Where was ‘The Fruits of the Monastic Life’ spoken?”

21.s: “Rājagahe, bhante, jīvakambavane”ti.
21.e: “In Jīvaka’s Mango Grove at Rājagaha.”

21.s: “Kena saddhin”ti?
21.e: “Who is it with?”

21.s: “Ajātasattunā vedehiputtena saddhin”ti.
21.e: “Ajātasattu Vedehiputta.”

21.s: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ sāmaññaphalassa nidānampi pucchi, puggalampi pucchi.
21.e: Mahākassapa also asked Ānanda about the origin story of ‘The Fruits of the Monastic Life’ and about the person.

21.s: Eteneva upāyena pañcapi nikāye pucchi. Puṭṭho puṭṭho āyasmā ānando vissajjesi.
21.e: In this way he asked about the five collections. Ānanda was able to reply to each and every question.

21.s: Atha kho āyasmā ānando there bhikkhū etadavoca— “bhagavā maṁ, bhante, parinibbānakāle evamāha— ‘ākaṅkhamāno, ānanda, saṅgho mamaccayena khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhaneyyā’”ti.
21.e: Ānanda said to the senior monks, “At the time of his final extinguishment, the Buddha said to me, ‘After my passing away, Ānanda, if the Sangha wishes, it may abolish the minor training rules.’”
21.t: 2. Discussion of the minor training rules (2. Khuddānukhuddakasikkhāpadakathā)

21.s: “Pucchi pana tvaṁ, āvuso ānanda, bhagavantaṁ— ‘katamāni pana, bhante, khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī’”ti?
21.e: “But, Ānanda, did you ask the Buddha what the minor training rules are?”

21.s: “Na khohaṁ, bhante, bhagavantaṁ pucchiṁ— ‘katamāni pana, bhante, khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī’”ti.
21.e: “No, sirs, I didn’t.”

21.s: Ekacce therā evamāhaṁsu— “cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā, avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī”ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṁsu— “cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā, terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā, avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī”ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṁsu— “cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā, terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā, dve aniyate ṭhapetvā, avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī”ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṁsu— “cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā, terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā, dve aniyate ṭhapetvā, tiṁsa nissaggiye pācittiye ṭhapetvā, avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī”ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṁsu— “cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā, terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā, dve aniyate ṭhapetvā, tiṁsa nissaggiye pācittiye ṭhapetvā, dvenavuti pācittiye ṭhapetvā, avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī”ti. Ekacce therā evamāhaṁsu— “cattāri pārājikāni ṭhapetvā, terasa saṅghādisese ṭhapetvā, dve aniyate ṭhapetvā, tiṁsa nissaggiye pācittiye ṭhapetvā, dvenavuti pācittiye ṭhapetvā, cattāro pāṭidesanīye ṭhapetvā, avasesāni khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī”ti.
21.e: Some senior monks said, “Apart from the four rules entailing expulsion, the rest are the minor training rules.” Others said, “Apart from the four rules entailing expulsion and the thirteen rules entailing suspension, the rest are the minor training rules.” Still others said, “Apart from the four rules entailing expulsion, the thirteen rules entailing suspension, and the two undetermined rules, the rest are the minor training rules.” Still others said, “Apart from the four rules entailing expulsion, the thirteen rules entailing suspension, the two undetermined rules, and the thirty rules entailing relinquishment and confession, the rest are the minor training rules.” Still others said, “Apart from the four rules entailing expulsion, the thirteen rules entailing suspension, the two undetermined rules, the thirty rules entailing relinquishment and confession, and the ninety-two rules entailing confession, the rest are the minor training rules.” Still others said, “Apart from the four rules entailing expulsion, the thirteen rules entailing suspension, the two undetermined rules, the thirty rules entailing relinquishment and confession, the ninety-two rules entailing confession, and the four rules entailing acknowledgment, the rest are the minor training rules.”

21.s: Atha kho āyasmā mahākassapo saṅghaṁ ñāpesi—
21.e: Then Venerable Mahākassapa informed the Sangha:

21.s: “Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho. Santamhākaṁ sikkhāpadāni gihigatāni. Gihinopi jānanti— ‘idaṁ vo samaṇānaṁ sakyaputtiyānaṁ kappati, idaṁ vo na kappatī’ti. Sace mayaṁ khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanissāma, bhavissanti vattāro— ‘dhūmakālikaṁ samaṇena gotamena sāvakānaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ paññattaṁ. Yāvimesaṁ satthā aṭṭhāsi tāvime sikkhāpadesu sikkhiṁsu. Yato imesaṁ satthā parinibbuto, na dānime sikkhāpadesu sikkhantī’ti. Yadi saṅghassa pattakallaṁ, saṅgho apaññattaṁ nappaññapeyya, paññattaṁ na samucchindeyya, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vatteyya. Esā ñatti.
21.e: “Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. We have training rules that relate to householders. The householders know what is allowable for us and what is not allowable. If we abolish the minor training rules, some people will say, ‘The ascetic Gotama laid down training rules for his disciples until the time of his death. But they practice the training rules only as long as their teacher is alive. Since their teacher has now attained final extinguishment, they no longer practice them.’ If the Sangha is ready, it shouldn’t lay down new rules, nor get rid of existing rules, and it should undertake to practice the training rules as they are. This is the motion.

21.s: Suṇātu me, āvuso, saṅgho. Santamhākaṁ sikkhāpadāni gihigatāni. Gihinopi jānanti— ‘idaṁ vo samaṇānaṁ sakyaputtiyānaṁ kappati, idaṁ vo na kappatī’ti. Sace mayaṁ khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadāni samūhanissāma, bhavissanti vattāro— ‘dhūmakālikaṁ samaṇena gotamena sāvakānaṁ sikkhāpadaṁ paññattaṁ. Yāvimesaṁ satthā aṭṭhāsi tāvime sikkhāpadesu sikkhiṁsu. Yato imesaṁ satthā parinibbuto, na dānime sikkhāpadesu sikkhantī’ti. Saṅgho apaññattaṁ nappaññapeti, paññattaṁ na samucchindati, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vattati. Yassāyasmato khamati apaññattassa appaññāpanā, paññattassa asamucchedo, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vattanā, so tuṇhassa; yassa nakkhamati, so bhāseyya.
21.e: Please, venerables, I ask the Sangha to listen. We have training rules that relate to householders. The householders know what is allowable for us and what is not allowable. If we abolish the minor training rules, some people will say, ‘The ascetic Gotama laid down training rules for his disciples until the time of his death. But they practice the training rules only as long as their teacher is alive. Since their teacher has now attained final extinguishment, they no longer practice them.’ The Sangha doesn’t lay down new rules, nor get rid of existing rules, and it undertakes to practice the training rules as they are. Any monk who approves of not laying down new rules, nor of getting rid of existing rules, and of undertaking to practice the training rules as they are should remain silent. Any monk who doesn’t approve should speak up.

21.s: Saṅgho apaññattaṁ nappaññapeti, paññattaṁ na samucchindati, yathāpaññattesu sikkhāpadesu samādāya vattati. Khamati saṅghassa, tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṁ dhārayāmī”ti.
21.e: The Sangha doesn’t lay down new rules, nor get rid of the existing rules, and it undertakes to practice the training rules as they are. The Sangha approves and is therefore silent. I will remember it thus.”

21.s: Atha kho therā bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavocuṁ— “idaṁ te, āvuso ānanda, dukkaṭaṁ, yaṁ tvaṁ bhagavantaṁ na pucchi—‘katamāni pana, bhante, khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī’ti. Desehi taṁ dukkaṭan”ti.
